chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Neither the Jew nor the Christian inherits the Muslim, and the Muslim inherits the Jew and the Christian.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits from whom: Muslims or People of the Book?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the asymmetrical inheritance rule where Muslims inherit from Jews and Christians, but not vice versa, reflecting the principle of 'preference of the higher status' (tarjih). In Shia jurisprudence, this is often linked to the spiritual and legal superiority of Islam, ensuring that the heir retains the faith of the deceased's superior religion. The ruling underscores the distinct legal boundaries maintained between the Muslim community and the People of the Book in matters of estate distribution.
